42E78DB95B4E486E98D2ECCF1CB3C7A8.description: Use different types of complete sentences to share information, give directions, or request information.

17BC84A309CF465F96FA337BA6262921.description: Use eye contact, volume, and tone appropriate to audience and purpose.

895C14C12D53431EB6B0BE5619EFEB2B.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

5B6B426EE9424BFB9DF555974A9DE367.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

C5F15C60AE8D45D8BB2A14F8850036A6.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

879FE85C297C44C692E1AABFFF543A09.description: Successful group activities need the cooperation of everyone.

AF87A1BD9E8B4A33B5BA08D246234BCF.description: Use grammatically correct language for the audience and specific vocabulary to communicate ideas and supporting details.

14977E612FD24C9EB1E5F72F80F3CD7C.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

C6C5C576CC5540F5A68055881F23294A.description: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

B9001F4591A3483892730EFCA6F23E03.description: Select and organize ideas sequentially or around major points of information that relate to the formality of the audience.

E3DCDFECC675450E9A47903FE76F8B40.description: Speak clearly, using appropriate volume and pitch for the purpose and audience.

51159F96B29148A58EF0378B3EE86281.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

23252503E35547128779EC0FF2333E5B.description: Oral communication is used both informally and formally.

C6A042193CAD457283814C702C4AE912.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

CB287DA915AE4E66B7B973B4B887479C.description: Explain that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.
comments: For example, all rectangles have four right angles and squares are rectangles, so all squares have four right angles.

88427D39D8D047039D8FD55E705FCC7B.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

9C7447E2461C49DABA5931DDAD1DF646.description: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

714881C256C64689A23682A324AB46D8.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
comments: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates.

Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., xaxis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

8DE342FADB4B471A982628AD6FF3C0DD.description: Geometric figures can be described by their attributes and specific locations in the plane.

2D9BFA7BB16445F5AB77032E9CC0F63D.description: Use the additive nature of volume to find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts.

7D69ABCF8EA447199CA934DCD426D172.description: Apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = b × h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths.

25E7A44DD05B43FCB096B49758B2FE59.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

02B3B9059A2A42AAB99E289C6C2C713F.description: Find volume of rectangular prisms using a variety of methods and use these techniques to solve real world and mathematical problems.

DBC7CABAD34A4F338D6272F795F466CC.description: Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes to represent the associative property of multiplication.

E45B433D65634A9FBD7CB0CA30AE8A4F.description: Show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base.

0C17F8C846C64715AD333161205960D6.description: Model the volume of a right rectangular prism with wholenumber side lengths by packing it with unit cubes.
comments: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume. A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

BAB07EE719284BF3B47DDF714CCB5BBF.description: Model and justify the formula for volume of rectangular prisms.

3C80073C77CB4703B11A6EDB7A1A9692.description: Properties of multiplication and addition provide the foundation for volume an attribute of solids.

comments: For example, given different measurements of liquid in identical beakers, find the amount of liquid each beaker would contain if the total amount in all the beakers were redistributed equally.

78D58A9386754CB1BC95C5923445946A.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8).

6A83D74BF29B4DD09E800825C21540DF.description: Visual displays are used to interpret data.

35C5232AC9224B33B79ED5BFF03ADB0B.description: Explain, extend, and use patterns and relationships in solving problems, including those involving saving and checking accounts such as understanding that spending more means saving less.

F128B5D855754E4E8092CFA6F5567889.description: Use patterns to solve problems including those involving saving and checking accounts.
comments: such as the pattern created when saving $10 a month

FFE0D0C16F03426899ADA3CE1BE552AD.description: Explain informally relationships between corresponding terms in the patterns.

3522BFE347DF4F59938EE5433E3884FF.description: Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graphs the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
comments: For example, given the rule "add 3" and the starting number 0, and given the rule "add 6" and the starting number 0, generate terms and the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence.

BB427070E5684CCE8327F8E5C84A296B.description: Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms.

2F4EEFC6EADE46E897AF77A562BB23B6.description: Generate two numerical patterns using given rules.

1527473020CD4B21827CB4A68505FE1A.description: Number patterns are based on operations and relationships.

132CFC3CF65F430E958673D3D444A3EA.description: Solve real world problems involving division of unit fractions by nonzero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions.
comments: e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. For example, how much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share 1/2 lb of chocolate equally? How many 1/3-cup servings are in 2 cups of raisins?

69A0E1216BD6404AB817A68ECC2B4E6D.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.
comments: For example, create a story context for 4 ÷ (1/5), and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 because 20 × (1/5) = 4.

5E18AA5C8EB34641AE41149FF82014D2.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.
comments: For example, create a story context for (1/3) ÷ 4, and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (1/3) ÷ 4 = 1/12 because (1/12) × 4 = 1/3.

7B16A4A5972D415E96F0A82B46C8E0E7.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers.
comments: e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

E2EF2B0CE29B4186A5E751C94353422F.description: Apply the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n × a)/(n × b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

C3052ABF54E2404D9110EC9763555025.description: Compare the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.
comments: Explain why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number.
Explain why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number.

825D520E62FA413B9B8D71D48A70FAF5.description: Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

BDAD0B7701FD41CDB2F7B686BE1A3FE5.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

48D9FBFE2F37442F9C613FF9F4CCCBB7.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b. In general, (a/b) × (c/d) = ac/bd.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to show (2/3) × 4 = 8/3, and create a story context for this equation. Do the same with (2/3) × (4/5) = 8/15.

171D4CFFBF404A188111E54461E52707.description: Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers.
comments: e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. For example, interpret 3/4 as the result of dividing 3 by 4, noting that 3/4 multiplied by 4 equals 3, and that when 3 wholes are shared equally among 4 people each person has a share of size 3/4. If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, how many pounds of rice should each person get? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

3B31D31E6B974F2A94B54723368044AC.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b).

5F7A662179394D56A6911F206B8A909A.description: The concepts of multiplication and division can be applied to multiply and divide fractions.

8E3C2DC85A91415D95C394C14FC612F5.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole.
comments: including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

C3B69704CF6441B2866AC7F652282A5A.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions with like denominators.
comments: in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators. For example, 2/3 + 5/4 = 8/12 + 15/12 = 23/12. (In general, a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd.).

62F84F38E4F94AB6A4D05AA0E401F3E1.description: Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.

B9354B85554742E3A99BAAD1D3C59270.description: Use strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division.

C25787B051AA4ADFAF2F7347269174D0.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

80FF39EE46964117B0EB334A7B8C555A.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

20F5873A8850469FBE8A0DDCEA07789C.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

45262CE6DE3D4DB6ABEB716107DEF05E.description: Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

EE1C5765B11247A18057CAD479248E51.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10.

DBE810D8DB864243A3388D23046699E1.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10.

C93F42DAC3AE4893A9D15129AC9FA7D0.description: Explain that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

document.title: Colorado Academic Standards for Reading, Writing, and Communicating

CC120464530F42A18F835B4E2157F23A.description: Evaluate the accuracy of the information in a text, citing text-based evidence, author's use of expert authority, and author's credibility to defend the evaluation.

34DF60B793FD4A19A495876FF8ADDA43.description: Analyze the logic (including assumptions and beliefs) and use of evidence (existing and missing information, primary sources, and secondary sources) used by two or more authors presenting similar or opposing arguments (such as articles by two political columnists that address the same issue).

76D2F8D4C77D446DBD15FB9DB06ED432.description: An author's reasoning is the essence of legitimate writing and requires evaluating text for validity and accuracy.

684610B27C484A9E822B7442CC48C236.description: Apply grades 9–10 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning").

E9DD668814D04EBE8EBE37B7832F4F3F.description: Apply grades 9–10 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work [e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare]").

37F9D97DB8CE4A93A7ECE57FA70B2514.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

81663A1A3BB04FEFB6275C1C35CDA2C5.description: Distinguish between types of evidence (e.g., expert testimony, analogies, anecdotes, statistics) and use a variety of types to support a particular research purpose.

D666A18B51AB4F148B0E32A012427E4F.description: Identify and evaluate potential sources of information for accuracy, reliability, validity, and timeliness.

39881C8E85B046E2B7F7CCED4842CFF5.description: Formulate research questions that are clear and precise.

2B3848E02B4049DC8B9A2A4DF23FBD6D.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

FF65A9CBA1FF4F53B03906E6B8238B4E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

D640D0743073415EB0DA3AD0C7F31A75.description: Collect, analyze, and evaluate information obtained from multiple sources to answer a question, propose solutions, or share findings and conclusions.

474D20EF4FB74C39946D1F484F3F1484.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

7C1133C1022443D19CB40DD2E8D9F62C.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

6E6A3D8233184C63BC95BF1A17A44ECB.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in expectations 1–2 above.)

77DB28A629204489AEE6D023F42C6044.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook, Turabian's Manual for Writers) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

8AA8B5410A0047708B4BB78D52C6EA98.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

14B65DC2F6DB4931A80A029124C7CD84.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

416306BC42B64809B3C307CD50D93B02.description: Use a semicolon (and perhaps a conjunctive adverb) to link two or more closely related independent clauses.

10A2780C955D43BC932B1D071AB29EDB.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional, absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent; noun, relative, adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

212605919AE045079F6C64622FE8545C.description: Distinguish between the active and passive voice, and write in the active voice.

83E6B7B2439E49E3B74339547683CC5C.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9A4BC53C6DAB434889C823B58FB080D9.description: Grammar, language usage, mechanics, and clarity are the basis of ongoing refinements and revisions within the writing process.

EB6DD27A89764F38812DE475FF0473C3.description: Present writing to an authentic audience and gauge effect on audience for intended purpose.

FD79CD2BD1534770BB4399C5640326AA.description: Explain how writers use organization and details to communicate their purposes.

25D98D6BB40A4DBBA8B0F41ED62B0DDA.description: Revise writing by evaluating relationship of central idea, evidence, and organizational pattern.

904995E7EB154EBAA5383E128A8FE887.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

636C1A567BFD469D98D98E02EAC354E3.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

49E43AE158314A0EBA39F23523855E29.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic.

BC6CB7E01C9A4D51A767A416F64A22A6.description: Collect, organize, and evaluate materials to support ideas.

9BB8630C9CC749F0912B195F3BBCB2BA.description: Choose and develop an effective appeal.

5A629939469943649554AE3422419FD5.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

05558C88E9C3417B9270FFFD4EAEBBCF.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

7DE7A69165D148868C1C718637459C71.description: Organizational writing patterns inform or persuade an audience.

BF3103AB19C54BAF8D266C7C52990BBA.description: Revise texts using feedback to enhance the effect on the reader and clarify the presentation of implicit or explicit theme.

1942336016A6432E98E6AEA408449A75.description: Use a variety of strategies to evaluate whether the writing is presented in a creative and reflective manner (e.g., reading the draft aloud, seeking feedback from a reviewer, scoring guides).

191C67ED78DC4AEA8FF9A348FE1D5444.description: Write literary and narrative texts using a range of stylistic devices (poetic techniques, figurative language, imagery, graphic elements) to support the presentation of implicit or explicit theme.

F943CFA6A55D4C8499606395B6B6664A.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

A2424122CF6C479188B33CB1E4CD715B.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

14E3B4CFAE7C421FB3B26BF356A44DF9.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

BDE73613E7DC4809B7284B53671B2D46.description: Literary or narrative genres feature a variety of stylistic devices to engage or entertain an audience.

CC0B482E853344D4956532DAE36EEB8F.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

A5B65B9D957A48D0A168430434C9C48E.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

33FEFDA79F5D464FB9D6D07BBE5C3326.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

142FFEFDE5B44D3E8AD5A0C9470668E2.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

325416DC7F4A49218E2E53882090AE03.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

EF7556D86C02448C83AED99B406A5027.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

5712180FE0284CAB90B3E6EC9289C581.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

59BCA90C841749F88954814AE78D7733.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

096F259CBE89461D96E30417DAFCD1DC.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution.

1DB8A3BE79244E95983F95FAD1D902ED.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

6F8655DDF9C945328DF1E04137AEEC33.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.
comments: For example, rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.

67C1DCD9CDA947E9B326A5118FFF4BB3.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.
comments: For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.

703ECD65F3374CBEA080682383AF88CC.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities and graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

7AE61DDB9AC74073A770934DE7F7086E.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems.
comments: Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

E263438EE6D7450CB7F54B9939709A15.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

54EDA4D6A5B94DFDB8BE3FE3831DA6A1.description: Solutions to equations, inequalities and systems of equations are found using a variety of tools.

B38C5F2341CE42C098D7BD3783E36B74.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms.
comments: write <sup>a(x)</sup>/b(x) in the form q(x) + <sup>r(x)</sup>/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

A6630152222C472A99EB32E46B6B64C6.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.
comments: For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)² = (x² – y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

523B2D81848046228D3DE3CDBDBC5207.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

B755DDA4273F47E197857495D882EBBD.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

BA7E275B4C014E3591B7B380BCEDC8BA.description: State and apply the Remainder Theorem.
comments: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

6500FA68CAC8499FADEE654F8B2F6747.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

A1B079F673D34575A1504217ACFB3562.description: Explain that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

1B655E0C57214D80B6B16AEAE7C92E69.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.
comments: For example, calculate mortgage payments.

78E31812B517464E8D64117E30AD97A8.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example the expression 1.15<sup>t</sup> can be rewritten as (1.15<sup>1/12</sup>)<sup>12t</sup> ≈ 1.012<sup>12t</sup> to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

D8C154D8AD1B44ADB64B47E3861AE3E5.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

C36CE300DADB4AB58CF12AEA852195E2.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

1D8801F65B1F4F85AD3BFB72B85DFB66.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

430E31A3273C45C58D03896A7116FCA6.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

7EF165A9D0824A75BFD8A65DE3979532.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x4 – y4 as (x2)2 – (y2)2, thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x2 – y2)(x2 + y2).

325AF40C4F074EB7B825090BAFE90CBC.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, interpret P(1+r)n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

59B09C88A72947119334884E8D870F50.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

E62A87E3B3594BA3AB347F2D1E5AA79F.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

684666F481C842C6BD362EE54F0AE4E7.description: Expressions can be represented in multiple, equivalent forms.

3FF580DC3C4A4A15B3810A0E8AB363F5.description: Analyze various lending sources, services, and financial institutions.

B230C3BCA52F434FB2B5C59391EE2D3E.description: Evaluate the costs and benefits of credit.

099C7544DF1A459EB8C067DC4632C1DF.description: Analyze the impact of interest rates on a personal financial plan.

E2EB203929E74F7EB7FA4BA0E79BB4FA.description: Choose the trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

D9FF2BC1B92D4E0C9EC5B67AFD43201B.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

34CAE76624E64F9FA57974529F0108A0.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

58E17A3D52C24544B82031D96F895767.description: Interpret expressions for function in terms of the situation they model.

2DF3820DDD1642DF8C307858CEF50F31.description: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to abct = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

AE88AB0749DF4AA8B91BAC2FCFC60354.description: Use graphs and tables to describe that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

271B833BC31E4A9B8CA0483AED69E079.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs.
comments: include reading these from a table.

D26C71B97FEF4DE2B21F33443ECFC7F8.description: Identify situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

ABA3CB427E8744058C093648493719E1.description: Identify situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

6E02BE8982084BAE86B558FB3A0DBAA6.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

5C382C7D0912450E967AC9B096C4DDC0.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

7534AC2435CC4138A4686B5A66162C65.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

3251B9268E59435CB5DA41598CE4D745.description: Quantitative relationships in the real world can be modeled and solved using functions

838629D14C3D497F8334FD2347DD3BD7.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

B60AADBECD4242E4BC1B07B96AFC1DB5.description: Use radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

902728787F8844E39900D7204E28A257.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

comments: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. For example, f(x) =2 x3 or f(x) = (x+1)/(x–1) for x ≠ 1.

3BCB81E55E32420A812132AD945E656D.description: Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology.

12B772974CFB4928838A4E2410327CB5.description: both positive and negative. Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k,9 and find the value of k given the graphs.
comments: Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

444AE94D14764ABAA017B194A2648403.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

EFF8504E39E848238BCC9DE1D4971C6C.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

884939275C144B749A339D39EC1FA0F6.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
comments: For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

6013EF61219141C790F148A311C00741.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

8CA02730F8CB46A1BB8C001A5BE459A9.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

6DE913D7B2714F17BF4C97EC49C99FEC.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

E4297D8622F048E0927C63A8015D0110.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.

6D6CA0DFBFF04E1B8E868DAAD008913F.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example, identify percent rate of change in functions such as y = (1.02)t, y = (0.97)t, y = (1.01)12t, y = (1.2)t/10,.

0F2BD6B2946D44FCA7F9FCCDFCC51596.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

044B85B1773E4C488CB705BD5E01FE89.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

9916280E3C534840A5A09C8EC4133A41.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

C28881B6B81F4C2CB25C071A621E14E2.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

988AF97C1D064BC882DA903D42B2957A.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

7894C6C1E60C4DA6BCCDE064795445E2.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

03B7E47379C748FC9560B00CCC34A2E7.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

83DF8A64713D41129481D1C39688D17A.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.
comments: presented symbolically or as a table.

4AF96ED7E7CB4C6C9E51AC4BF5A4C9ED.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.
comments: For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.

83FBED7304F0486296D76A90B1B5DA45.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship.
comments: Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

64BAE318EE2F406BB06C3A9953D4A442.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

17AE6AB50AE54D299037EDE5FF9A21F8.description: Demonstrate that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.
comments: For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n) + f(n-1) for n ≥ 1.

F69AC9D77AE5422FAA240F56D3314EC3.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

3308F7C5A5C84AB49C6E385CAD7EA58A.description: Explain that a function is a correspondence from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) that assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range.
comments: If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

4C0A1103C35249338980570ED21E6A26.description: Formulate the concept of a function and use function notation.

59D9418FE5F346C5A24F43668B08D520.description: Functions model situations where one quantity determines another and can be represented algebraically, graphically, and using tables.

6777500AE0924CA4813616CE68BED365.description: Design and use a budget, including income (net takehome pay) and expenses (mortgage, car loans, and living expenses) to demonstrate how living within your means is essential for a secure financial future

37FF0460E73544BABD1D7189C69FC65F.description: Describe factors affecting take-home pay and calculate the impact

2BB7ABD46BB74F2594556F4A3EF3AA76.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

0C26EB2DE37A4797830749ECB97518F4.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

26B60A8643DE43E9AB85C1452FFC0C88.description: Choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

F7ABB907C8FB4085A3F8F0BE7FEC7938.description: Choose and interpret units consistently in formulas.

3EF9AA4EF4414B8387337F5C843B035C.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems.

FC2910B776B44416AD5D5ABFBC451279.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

A625066B5BB345D8BB318EFC692148EA.description: Quantitative reasoning is used to make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations.

DD865FC6FD584B30B92FC3D59AAB5AF2.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

82869B8D59714006865F991CB3A5FC9B.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

9B76A63511A44E72AC4BD0E2E8EF316F.description: Use the relation i² = –1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

B60771C62D4240788C1F15738E046288.description: Define the complex number i such that i² = –1, and show that every complex number has the form a + bi where a and b are real numbers.

AEF356341244477AAA82410E5EE891FA.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

0B765AAD6B024ADAAB969C99F21A312C.description: Explain why the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

D544F5B385AD4E26ACAAA9C360EC5396.description: Explain why the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

8555FD00E3134835BB993E7CA79ABA5A.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational.

FBD277714656446A965BE206D18FE502.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

7F58663A937A4892B34CE731CE86E745.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

7D5046E131184DB39C95A7290A55F4D5.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.
comments: For example, we define 5<sup>1/3</sup> to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ = 5(<sup>1/3</sup>)³ to hold, so (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ must equal 5.

9FB084948DCE48C9A14D254F09777860.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

A7F74D14D65E44B7AD6E3C5CD8F6636C.description: The complex number system includes real numbers and imaginary numbers.

document.title: Colorado Academic Standards for Reading, Writing, and Communicating

1543E03DDACE41AD8895993CE914CD8F.description: Evaluate information for clarity and accuracy.

C9CF10A5BF11479DBBA34FEF3101F43A.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

CA1DAFBB68174C3997FEF4A3973F084F.description: Identify a clear and significant purpose for research (Is my purpose for researching frogs clear and is it important to understanding more about mammals?).

EAB93E6CB27F492FB1650D28BA388613.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of "how-to" books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).

4305814CEF194656937114444CCC8A1E.description: Purpose, information, and questions about an issue are essential steps in early research.

D4F22898B8E0419DBD491F43091D4B99.description: Use text features (titles, illustrations, headings, bold type) to locate, interpret, and use information.

8A8F13119BFC4DF5A0C03FB1A78CCC1F.description: With peers, use a variety of resources (direct observation, trade books, texts read aloud or viewed) to answer questions of interest through guided inquiry.

272D29BF23124655997A4D3F7E913E19.description: Write or dictate questions for inquiry that arise during instruction.

105C155881294F6B83CA0F0FA17BE99E.description: A variety of resources leads to locating information and answering questions of interest.

CBDBDA9FB8CE4A419AA484FB6299D9DE.description: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.

77CFF81F95C449A998DF4E4BFDC95DE7.description: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.

7EF311A2D5584AA9A714DCFD47B8B7D5.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

A6DEC26276F44488BC1D9A7E15C51BF3.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

39D64542DF8B428BBC735A6CEAFBAC0F.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

CA9F3E77558A4737BAC70C3CF2471D3C.description: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.

D3B79B1CE8F5410CB47AEC05707FCF6B.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).

6B805FBD03A84BB7BFC15641176101DC.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).

0BD8F7C3BB7E49A4BD083EF162AD6DB4.description: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).

21EB25A65B3B40AAA0C5B517536014A5.description: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their, anyone, everything).

26DC7FECD3A94DB99FC806EDE4EB87A7.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).

FFBC05821B03422DBF2C554EFC5DC56F.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

1FFD47EE104B424D864871837DE3FE91.description: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.

B48E18763E46423F8331E7437586F8A3.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

E749AC8658E0423AAAE0C7BCAFF2831C.description: Appropriate spelling, conventions, and grammar are applied when writing.

CB26C1CD7E864BB2BA3927F7D1D27B4E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

765194382CF5415CB6D8C3D881DD7B76.description: Use pictures or graphic organizers to plan writing.

AEB7C568E90B407A9F9329511766B115.description: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

83FD4BA9EFF44DA5B21489C89E76E699.description: Write narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure.

DEFB5F19712D4CC79ACE9E629B561D54.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.

E1F70C18240C4E5CA92AB7BF5CCAF421.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.

8CF0246968284CFCB92F8934B093A200.description: Exploring the writing process develops ideas for writing texts that carry meaning.

68B982E7436D4326AA89AC48CBD8F574.description: Create new words by combining base words with affixes to connect known words to new words.

05C5558CEBFB49F6948A2D3BB6A2A330.description: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).

B7EA1545E8854A54A758FA9E71ED1671.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

6165DFEA8D6D49DD880D3B60794B9B09.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).

44CECB57A16E47D3B2CE2396CB21DF66.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.

5DA9E4E469BD4428A333B2CBDE13B3CC.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).

1B21FB47E62A46588272A812FCD8FBB5.description: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).

57DC8E6208554E8ABE2305F510EAAB3A.description: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

AC1EA8226D9C4B7FBBB5B093E1507CEF.description: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

E6230B1002EE4DC08B6779197BF25FF3.description: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, looking).

B200E0A7E2C54FD1A6D526DE1FC17438.description: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.

1D93C0EC803B4DA692431400D2948C6F.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

679C99E611A14A08BF937BA011A441E8.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

196300BBA66D441998AF05012362D6C2.description: Understanding word structure, word relationships, and word families needs to be demonstrated to begin to read.

BEC85C5FA6EC4C3F98B1B69C07783DED.description: Accurately decode unknown words that follow a predictable letter/sound relationship.

38BA38D2852B4D539C43CCECE2DC119E.description: Use onsets and rimes to create new words (ip to make dip, lip, slip, ship).

A5516FD4062140429C81DEB0D370D3AD.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

9AD63F907B824B74B791EA7388276244.description: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.

66170F4EFBC1463084E7AE2E772C5EAD.description: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.

53A3DEEDBB804F7AA8B27770B31F34F0.description: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.

3E6EE9E4725243ED9744FF7765059055.description: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs (two letters that represent one sound).

1BF2C0F15610490E9F9A0AAEED77564A.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

B7D565439B464021B18BD3F44F89A33B.description: Decoding words require the application of alphabetic principles, letter sounds, and letter combinations.

1305E7BA9C094C7A98AE3589F408F84F.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

DEEA7A486BA848DDA214E12B926B911E.description: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.

021DAD38C9EE4E34BB958C0B63E5A63B.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

069770E90708418DA45CCB6A8707B0C0.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

E79C28DBC3874FD38DDE39165E2D80BF.description: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.

0101F9F402A445EB85AF2432E8D1C52C.description: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:

2F953E3B9E6E4688AA3D879283305274.description: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

09C84B3742F64FFCAEAFE74F32AEF55D.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

2A767E464A844F68912899DE2CA4C3AA.description: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.
