2FF51733410F403CB4EAF4A1415957B8.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.

A77A528B74D3422A89D4B28FF5401269.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

E7A86F79949242AB8A907F8FC44117C5.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

61DB6F33E81F4564992C580D4A9B0924.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

7851B27AF90345F48ED31B4A78863653.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

FB19F01EF70E4A41A1817F12C8823D34.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

B751AADE13224276905CF42E58E0A102.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

AAB225C6DEDB482DAC0E2AB0B0D12570.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.

1A0132998DB544B5A5D4FFDC705C923B.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

95E0800A7AFA48B5BF96FBA0889E4A49.description: Define a function as a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. Show that the graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output. (Function notation is not required for Grade 8.)

79C3AE920F4F42BEBE5832F11FB9BFFB.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.

98F200A15F5A4D2E88B7CCBD504119D1.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.

A6AECBDBE3B14292BA41B8E08DC38E9A.description: Explain that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

D53F92A5D97743D9BC11254538617A2E.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

30E63D6FCDCD48209D8459255667F24B.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations with variables on both sides and whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

B4E41B5C97274D12AA5CAFB0D4E45D32.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

A7812F16DF2F4844B32DE488DCF832D1.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

9AFCF1EA66C04244AAD8F5317FA537CD.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

B0AE59FC41EB4F968FF5A8AE040A9361.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

C72E1236FDCA43A98B336AC844C5EE42.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.

9BD53CCE231641B1A809D284CBCB303D.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

FF2D217EB2F9403FA00F96914E1D7019.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

543A31CD102B4E05B11C5736C278220C.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other. For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 times 108 and the population of the world as 7 times 109, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.

3B9CADF18D6F457CB7495EDA2A3F2F39.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares (up to 100) and cube roots of small perfect cubes (up to 64). Know that √2 is irrational.

3696159DE316437A8250AED25C6B8F00.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.

99B565E7EC2141A98D0F2692F794E38F.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

9FF3861085784D53A0FD8C3D4AF5FBAE.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).

07FD7F13E8D441CBAE1574C5B3F622AA.description: Demonstrate informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number. Define irrational numbers as numbers that are not rational.

EDB3D8851B7C43118A1E807677C75A06.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

7723087000924D4DBBD7D80CE26BBEE1.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

05B6F423F96A4D41992F0BE6B62EBD57.description: Look for and make use of structure.

99E8AFBBFBC946B8BA65790AE98718D4.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

46DB30F8A04741188983DAFD8A4D6BB4.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

62440B900BCE4A65A270184CF4DDCB54.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

3CF02AD6FFA2458BBC928754A21AAE0A.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

E5396D91F79841DA8B32E5361752F536.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

801944D08B584105A295546FECA1CA4A.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

C6157015560C40FD85765138A1DB2ECC.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

BF037C57AC704AE7830A3A91D716E528.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

729784FDEAEE44C3BE958A90AEBDA9D6.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

28F2E2B3B4B14944B1B030A8F687F52E.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

573C45E7A9ED4976BF4F413E59E79BF0.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

5DF8A2C26D4945689746220AB266433E.description: Understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

E7966FCE504843419DA7A941FF2ED73C.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

F50182B59BEC48DBBF66E94A2475A532.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world and mathematical problems.

14630B403B644BE8914D57AE8EA58D58.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

B2F727C3763641BB95B024FCE041EE68.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.

9B430747ECCA45648889CBEFC4373E28.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

A3F117E490FF4AB3842608A2F4BE1CD3.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.

CACCB67DEF2A42CEB73C010BBB9A640E.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.

23A48C69C2384338934F0C37AF350CC4.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

AC9D2ED88E05465CBE3658DA80F7FD6B.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

2728734F360C4894922570BA5B80A4A3.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

19505DBA54D5437BAA61838A7E85A911.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35=5×7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

1A7E13D1003B4ACCAD62B6C23CF90600.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

8D4F20DADEDA4CC5A59260A257EC0413.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

747DB053A889497C9D4EB54AC487E0B4.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

254AF30429854F1EB108950615CC9894.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100. (Students who can generate equivalent fractions can develop strategies for adding fractions with unlike denominators in general. But addition and subtraction with unlike denominators in general is not a requirement at this grade.)

33031B5F328845CDAAB0E277A0280ECD.description: Use decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

648F2FCBD17D4C9FBA31E45EA9282CF7.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

6BAB19459B714DDDB623DB7DA68CDCCA.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

A702545787494EE9AB8250D8AC3C2193.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.

39DD9DE3BAC04B708D94F26FBFB2697B.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

F9BE9D602AF2492CB3EF276FACB5363A.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

2458B29F5E3748B9876D340CAE2576AD.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

68836F638BF44942A174C17CFC8942B8.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with like denominators in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

C8053D2CF19F44EE86479B67F3DDA393.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

0D06ECB23C4F4BF280DFDC7285919FBC.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a>1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

B15A8DCEEEFC42D5ACA39069E650311C.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

047D393109EE4A4C9002B6FCB728932A.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction n×a/n×b by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

4F23926BA1F54B649D5939D552FC2B07.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

E56A9643882C418196C2210E728677DC.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

BECFCDBFB5EA470D8026789B41EEF375.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

F570B6E5D5F540FC8D161E5C927435ED.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

7B8D29E3567E4C12BAF8060EEA56356A.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

ADD2D26FB97F4E8D924B11EF8A52A9A3.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

5FFC1C142206460184E3CF19C2EAC831.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

B9C26D59A84A4907AF14D12FC237C4AB.description: Explain that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

4F33EC2DEE204F2E96C237462DFFD0C2.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

8FD226B58F6D441BABE66C1D40A50FFF.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

7C608DDCD3E347E4B38E45EA526744B5.description: Look for and make use of structure.

BCB9634ED80343FD8A11972CDEBC2DF4.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

CF398AB91FB24F9C83A595CA28541D79.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

4D8B5DAA41C14E4D89CFF6EABD389ECA.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

CD97EDF0936C404B9F4078AD470E7EE3.description: Explain that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.

D13C1E3D2BE0430A838DA123291447CE.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

75B61D7DD9D74F11A71ED852D18003E6.description: Represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

91FA584277D348A2B0B3DC0C6BCD2517.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

6E7A309251EA4482B0566AE334740968.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

21502C308E2149B989E85CFEBE9BBCDF.description: Use the additive nature of volume to find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.

41490BBA5FCF478195FEE358C777681A.description: Apply the formulas V=l×w×h and V=b×h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

6EC9C976A89D4E69A7A4F9CE3CFBAE7E.description: Model the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

EE43A67B8EA24A84B5DD733B92CBF82D.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume.

83C8FB14BEDF453A9893AA321BD24591.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

E38495341A474CD7A6958A1B6619B80A.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

AF66874C0AEE49DC96E61531CB201D1B.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume and can be used to measure volume.

9347D465CF984571A2BA4A5D76DC72FF.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

679D9BF39C3E458C8B96EE02CCE672AD.description: Understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

911638BB88044B9CA739308D561DCC8A.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots.

5A79143678B549FCB9EE980A833D5A10.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real-world problems.

3D4BBB22BF3C45B799B6D35083017C18.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

D07D27182344474C9C425F3E4D418727.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

5DE9ADECC194480395B89A8A6EF78B43.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

E3291B2701CD4557A3E711317372F3C3.description: Use grouping symbols (parentheses, brackets, or braces) in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

4A8D6A1E980B488298B41EC0D22ED0E8.description: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

342C0ADDFE5D4F79A7BE25D17E60D971.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.

032D14A8E0DC4CF7B680B2F2918F5C36.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.

BE9682CDC92645C6B7781B1FB6E5DA06.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions. (Students able to multiply fractions in general can develop strategies to divide fractions in general, by reasoning about the relationship between multiplication and division. But division of a fraction by a fraction is not a requirement at this grade.)

8368899B77684BA18DFF0A2B5EB62E75.description: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

554A9F59084D4B639C55643DA1A8DD6D.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b=n×a/n×b to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

1319F1AB28314103B5243657ECB26D27.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

38FD9AB54E2949AC837D2CF30D024461.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

4A3C7A5D080B40BBBD1A0E1CB813C362.description: Interpret the product a/b×q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a×q÷b.

094E507379BD46BA86C10BA219B37A18.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

48F4D73A6C1E4CB69FDECF98A60537D8.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b=a÷b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

43D3DAE8402E4CFBAC036F9ABAEA14A7.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division.

4F123FB9A2544723B61092B5BDC7D29D.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.

8C7F9497B0F54289AA558AE175033956.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.

1889ED6BB4354C6BB6F05182FD362C36.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

4B73CDADB10B48E79E2E89487B487AF8.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

CEA22C2136574AE5813BA960F6582AD2.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

8C1984A749014CE4919798DA979DD29E.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

A0A73FDFE74548648856A41C0C5FE867.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

6307B27F4DE04A5FB699AA524139FBD4.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

A5EEB51B2E694564A82B71F8A9770FFB.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

3BF5944CBD634CC893B8EF74153DA58F.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., 347.392=3×100+4×10+7×1+3×110+9×1100+2×11000.

67446D646DF2447FB04949986DC115B3.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

B858057C298B435199C49EEC410B42D8.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

6649CF7FD4BC4254AB1A162E035C186C.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

C4700ED1D49B4D3C866125EB7620B17E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

8EEA0D83108A43B29D9DA1ABF2C42C03.description: Look for and make use of structure.

E30732890C8D4BE0B731A5EB7B47A81E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

E0314165E442451181F7E07267D1FB56.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

2B7B6FC62B6A45E2A7A721B8548A1E73.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

54E7525EC38442A29F491D1E36D674ED.description: Explain that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

8452820578984B03A13D2EC6CB1F2156.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

C959979A42FD414A8436E660A3EB7E64.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

F0316BDE04DE4CD2A3B16D9B68BF11B0.description: Recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

EA7B24676D7541729ED153D041DED09B.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b+c is the sum of a×b and a×c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

B54384D05A4F46708E35EF58FB6BF59D.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

25FC32E584F54E68B82648FCB9D3F3C8.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

CB158695A72549228065A70CC1412CD0.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

0C498516AF79425B94A1DD381DFB2D63.description: Use concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

42AB10BCDDEB45DEA8B1F5A62319B2FE.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

388110451A534CCFBF7CA48AC0874C14.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

BAEF004CB42D41C6BEC1A847663AFBA9.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

4B14A3F3085943448A674BE5B41D6E28.description: (+) Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

C46C559A1E5241A898AEB4DCF03D9623.description: (+) Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

A4FE576ECD7D4A64A86A403E9BBADD25.description: Represent and model with vector quantities.

C74D063EACB549A282E41F538B0DB2E3.description: (+)Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

F7D6253A9BFA4934A17E4D2128BFAAB5.description: (+)Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.

E672DB6D64E4435287CC4E064DFC9A2C.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

508BD8D4F9E74CC2BA18B3FB7CD4A654.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

9D424C91A0844ED79FA44F308F4579A6.description: (+) Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

3F76A59C0B9D4184A9BBD768924B01A2.description: (+) Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.

BA8462258E5645D1A09EC9FC17CE9646.description: (+) Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

60D3451E6425426AABFE3AC707817A8E.description: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.

F6FE478E8F7B468992F1818E62108C1B.description: (+) Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli and quotients of complex numbers.

6D387F16B24945488951EE70CA932B46.description: Use the relation i² and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

48AFBBC438B4422F97AE68CA6E83866E.description: Define complex number i such that i² = -1, and show that every complex number has the form a + bi where a and b are real numbers.

7F3F0CD2BFA040599DE4D1B7A4001BDC.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

9DBFD4F9B9734E8BBF6B1C8C2CEA64D8.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

23C85BD3DBD84463977A2CE37F206F52.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

FB6B046E7713464B9E3FD65269761483.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

C1D5C74B76474580AC2D49C5858E7B12.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

F9D39F4092234317935AC4B8810EEEC1.description: (+) Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

3A3F6AC797B94BBDAFF0A9C62B9415BB.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

9421795973074AC2920AF7894B23501E.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

BFFC2C449878452DB6ED38535323A54B.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.

FDDBBD6CCA0F4B8D8FDD55A31FC40CDF.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

E55227AD00224B10AC51E8DD65EDD84D.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

0A725D32CC984FD5800D3BAA42EF5A4C.description: Look for and make use of structure.

6462D8AB47D744E7BD69545E769EB6C3.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

2D953E3F47914F44BE0F74629D0ECDB2.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Colorado Academic Standards: Reading, Writing and Communicating

027C8BC571434F318CFEB58A3876BCE4.description: Identify problems and search for solutions by asking questions during collaborative explorations of the topic; begin to state facts about the topic.

13F14B769FEE4264B1A342BC9FF9683E.description: Begin research by asking a question to identify and define a problem and its possible solutions.

1C9A95E94D4D42E59827745515F8D35E.description: Copy, trace, or independently write letters or words.

0077FC2DD9184946829F900479990EB5.description: Use scribbles, shapes, pictures, and letters to represent objects, stories, experiences, or ideas.

31CA2BFC58EF4325A7700A704F6BAF8F.description: Recognize that writing is a way of communicating for a variety of purposes, such as giving information, sharing stories, or giving an opinion.

B3AD8A16505C40AAAC35777C3CC91E95.description: Experiment with writing tools and materials.

F0F0C8706D414B4CB6D62A30BD150F43.description: Familiarity with writing implements, conventions, and emerging skills to communicate through written representations, symbols, and letters.

BD1168D064AB4E7AAF70BD004A79ADC6.description: Identify letters and associate correct sounds with letters, including a minimum of ten letters, preferably including letters in the child's name.

ADB22EF546FA47CAA40165CFCF3C97C4.description: Attend to the beginning letters and sounds in familiar words.

A75313A04955405791B0FDABE6AA0637.description: Recognize that letters of the alphabet have distinct sound(s) associated with them.

2E7633E0583B437E816FA3BA6370FE69.description: Recognize that the letters of the alphabet are a special category of visual graphics that can be individually named.

19CCF0E9345449D0B30C0530F8DB71E7.description: The names and sounds associated with letters makes up alphabetic knowledge.

FEDC82883117430A814FA69A61EC7F07.description: Recognize the association between spoken or signed and written words.

AA58636F8A7D4E88834A2B36FBAE4995.description: Recognize words as a unit of print and understand that letters are grouped to form words.

3CA3D1571F4B4F80B8270DFF790D98F9.description: Understand conventions, such as print moves from left to right and top to bottom of a page.

800257C3193E4EDBADE36B2254BA097D.description: Recognize print in everyday life, such as numbers, letters, one's name, words, and familiar logos and signs.

42CA9C655D6D4074863F669C3189FBEC.description: Print concepts and conventions anchor concepts of early decoding.

243B961FD0AB420CA7553AB8A8C64D89.description: Recognize patterns of sounds in songs, storytelling, and poetry through interactions and meaningful experiences.

1839E5AB1E63496B9AD90F093D8AC4B5.description: Identify and discriminate between sounds and phonemes in language, such as attention to beginning and ending sounds of words and recognition that different words begin or end with the same sound.

9D744FCF267D4E4797ED3A3CAD7ED658.description: Identify and discriminate between separate syllables in words.

473FA0FE39D64D5EACFAAEBC3259A676.description: Identify and discriminate between words in language.

67202F31C2584809BB08BA9A0F50B537.description: Phonological awareness is the building block for understanding language.

8269218FAC9E4DB4833631A38CB69B4B.description: Begin to identify key features of reality versus fantasy in stories, pictures, and events.

E3B9EBDCF0814C4E96358313CBD49ADC.description: Retell stories or information from books through conversation, artistic works, creative movement, or drama.

9D72770D108049AC872B844D35533CA4.description: Begin to identify key features of reality versus fantasy in stories, pictures, and events.

A5D9411165E447FDB3920DCF72895C5C.description: Demonstrate interest in different kinds of literature, such as fiction and nonfiction books and poetry, on a range of topics.

2CCE6CD595F94AF8BC2E6CD5DC599A45.description: Ask and answer questions and make comments about print materials.

0667AA1BE5D74AB7A7827D231B0B57AB.description: Recognize how books are read, such as front-to-back and one page at a time, and recognize basic characteristics, such as title, author, and illustrator.

C80705853C354C9E91248F875BF23EDC.description: Show interest in shared reading experiences and looking at books independently.

8C100C939724436C8F9AE5D19FDC1D6F.description: Children understand and obtain meaning from stories and information from books and other texts.

A014D780CFFC43E7AB65D7DAA23156C6.description: Speak in sentences of five or six words.

151D0F890A774550A7A73C2D2C74EE85.description: Practice asking questions and making statements.

AF4354670924414CA1110BC4DAE4EC69.description: Understand the difference between a question and a statement.

2BCE24E3C85D409B960C9F9D7968C6E7.description: Use increasingly complex and varied vocabulary.

D99DFDC5666C409FBF4429767495B016.description: Use language to express ideas and needs.

21A317601916435EBDA2E559EEC198B9.description: Participate in conversations of more than three exchanges with peers and adults.

06CA6CB8C95D459295935F5C3B59D4A7.description: Children use language to convey thoughts and feelings.

02A76BF02D044B968E5F9E5C15343088.description: Comprehend increasingly complex and varied vocabulary.

CBDE3BC2D97D4D9BBB9B488F6253BF6F.description: Attend to language during conversations, songs, stories or other learning experiences.

35FB93C97353480F905DB75F5197EAE7.description: Children comprehend and understand the English language.

document.title: Colorado Academic Standards: Reading, Writing and Communicating

263000AF66144C89849EA878F5743D58.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (for example: "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text").

737C420CA84A46C38DF1932F1516EB01.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (for example: "Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [for example: a character's thoughts, words, or actions].").

B1765B037AA74C89BCBF496886D7E372.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

FE9AF1189D9E44F6BFC2F1E3B23280CC.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.

ABBF0955A4D744DF8F981AA1685C2F95.description: Present a brief report of the research findings to an audience.

A01C9D66343A484FBB592A643906AB85.description: Identify a topic and formulate open-ended research questions for further inquiry and learning.

A6D9FB7827D24BF4846E13EA3C72703F.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

A12AE62F9D8F40268998D1BF98C7B434.description: Use a variety of resources to build and communicate knowledge related to open-ended research questions.

1C686BC91FB34F11907742AF3D22065C.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

465992E2771746C584F775F0D370D661.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.

6E7F85C20B75402B889F8B32CD57C1D5.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

50A01D4F4059473BBC556AA3900E33B2.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

35020A19C8414B0491A80B5C3CD58712.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (for example: presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (for example: small-group discussion).

258AA09080BB4E4A90B00CA2ED140015.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

9F0FC49A657D4CD0B77361A97BA81720.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

93E37C582E65443894A788226A73390B.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

AC7626D6B16C49C5B6CB1494B3C4AAF3.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

63D84DC866B94BB991C6D91306F25B1C.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

A2633326FD9A443EA7D892E67296196F.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

22492DA041814F6A9420377ED0B34A66.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (for example: to, too, two; there, their)

41B3FC25CB7B4000B9C270BFA7FB79F4.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

8B78329C7F39461A8A3AB53E344A91BA.description: Produce complete simple, compound, and complex sentences.

F2FF70CAA6C04A0594E5D06DFBAB2ADC.description: Use compound subjects (for example: Tom and Pat went to the store) and compound verbs (for example: Harry thought and worried about the things he said to Jane) to create sentence fluency in writing

71A12161F5FB46E4834672E9A1732E53.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (for example: a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

41A2A5DEB3954852835DC794ED92D17A.description: Use modal auxiliaries (for example: can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

C7CB9791D38E461183ECBA89E0C3169A.description: Form and use the progressive (for example: I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

6DD77A849EF34067854D6BC95A6BDEFB.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

7B6B9090257E49F28ADF3F4D8B37300C.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

F419854A1C8C40499E31D24F99A58E30.description: Understand why and how writers use the conventions of Standard English grammar, usage, and mechanics to clarify their meaning.

3A5F7EA4EB524E76B820BFF99334D712.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

CC3BF206049F438DBE8E7E5C189F58AE.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

3938D557007E427E92B3C0BDDF2C2B30.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.

2749AB5BFE2244EBAA56491291C8D572.description: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

8BBD431ECF414FC986DFFDDB16774081.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

5109F77880624549B1326D1164326639.description: Write engaging, real or imagined narratives using descriptive details and dialogue to convey a sequence of related events.

6F11538356E6485BB4A25A31970EDA6A.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.

F8473F88A93B4E02892FF0CB95E86622.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

76888D5B72B04C80A51BED3869EA3772.description: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (for example: another, for example, also, because).

1CEA02D4CA314731ADBC52D546F3CC99.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

E3A72E5A1DB546CE9481D909C2E99D3B.description: Organize relevant ideas and details to convey a central idea or prove a point.

5D7488396729498FBD0B2AF16C2BE69D.description: Identify a text structure appropriate to purpose (sequence, chronology, description, explanation, and comparison-and-contrast).

25B24AC0691A4EC4BB3495223BD92FB8.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (for example: headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

06595F429BDF41AEB57CD923083EBF51.description: Write informative/explanatory texts using text structures appropriate for the purpose and developed through facts, definitions, concrete details, precise language, and domain-specific vocabulary.

900FDC7CF14F434883F50641026BFB05.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

86B7D035E1974BD0AD33612800EBDC77.description: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (for example: for instance, in order to, in addition).

56C629078E8B495FAAF3EEA1293CDC2D.description: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.

57A848B69E1F4D0095B4D4B5A8D6B79B.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.

8547F55E5A234F89AE5AEEC11347DB24.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts supporting a point of view with reasons and information.

E34F63AF17E64914BA77F62B2A2749B6.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (for example: quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (for example: wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

BD2A48FA18D8483493A8E503C5134F22.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

F818F33A17A84E1F8BE2AC709AAC9DA8.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

8F92499007164E4694D9CBCFD5C956E3.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (for example, as pretty as a picture) in context.

0181C9A095D7411E919520AC12C789A5.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

0EED124C38B941E89061DCA1F005D9D9.description: Consult reference materials (for example: dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

A3348E460EF44BB581ED457E110C4FA1.description: Infer meaning of words using explanations offered within a text.

4C63F23A302F4C0EA440EEC5EE652E85.description: Read multisyllabic words with and without inflectional and derivational suffixes

B385B903F7A64823AEFE790AC6AEE70C.description: Read and understand words that change spelling to show past tense (for example: write/wrote, catch/caught, teach/taught)

2E6F583E6CB54A21AC9FE3CBFB253978.description: Read and understand words with common prefixes (for example: un-, re-, dis-) and derivational suffixes ( for example: -ful, -ly, -ness)

2BDC54DE184C41EAB8A7A9C6821F0BF5.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (for example: telegraph, photograph, autograph).

4B17E3E1F63A44508F67320944AFF00D.description: Use context (for example: definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

DC4481E48C1F493C9EDB4751EAA23A74.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

5A459B33DE5440BC9E795F42DB1E305F.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

01D53E0E417C4C5D927A0232446B9F47.description: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.

3AA05CB46D6748668AD99058DC069DA4.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

627E8D8945A64E0EBB29BD89384DFCC2.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

4B08E8447AD1463F9E9EF0573BC55212.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (for example, roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

7B86AF74F940426B82622BE3AD125345.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

CE88D79AC9D1479189CC6D6B4CE275DA.description: Apply knowledge of spelling patterns (orthography) and word meanings (morphology) to decode multisyllable words and determine the meaning of unknown words.

8025426A0A3449888AA5EA2087420A5A.description: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 4–5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

64D1D5F1E7DF4671B38E33B29AD4878F.description: Use Range of Reading and Complexity of Text to:

F1A341B456CA4BE996CBCE3746C9F1F8.description: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

FC97B17EB0964C46B3F0E8D1906CB037.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.

85BA86ACFC274532825E8FBC78DCED5E.description: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (for example: in charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, animations, or interactive elements on Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.

495E7D0C47BE4635A4083D2CDDF432E2.description: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:

5D5242F0F1E146FCABC81A6365694B7A.description: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.

958C8D938885489BB055F6A6058BA1DD.description: Describe the overall structure (for example, chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.

9541340E3C53489D8DA111DE108B9816.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.

E7DDDC48A44D4BBB891707558BE173B1.description: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.

FF34111E6991486B829CC1CD1F38DD09.description: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.

5BB1368D654B4A1B9F7D24588C446B35.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

DE20AC71FA25437ABC1025A603C95E0E.description: Use Key Ideas and Details to:

0676907BA841480E9AE19CF50FA0616B.description: Apply strategies to comprehend and interpret informational texts.

19C8AC11B5A2466E99CB9906CD838B7D.description: Read familiar texts orally with fluency, accuracy, and prosody (expression).

5E95E203314640489BFD63D84DA4B5A0.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

3A754742C1304231BB7C4300844064A7.description: Use Range of Reading and Complexity of Text to:

CF57E7160836415DA5A3B5CFACFE1390.description: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (for example: opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (for example: the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.

FBC9052526D8404889959E9B6F5B392E.description: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.

F7EAF1513A7842C896FE29248050322C.description: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:

200F7C9D77C34013A75E4E3AF88E610C.description: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.

F792560C736F48FFB500CF894FD4BA9C.description: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems (for example: verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (for example, casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.

826B7A5F76BF43E4BB07230FCA30B4C1.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (for example: Herculean).

6E25906530AE48E29C36A0478FEBE799.description: Describe the development of plot (such as the origin of the central conflict, the action of the plot, and how the conflict is resolved).

EFDF2994D6824C6BAACDF264759CD2A6.description: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (for example: a character's thoughts, words, or actions).

D9A99D0A487B4819A5AB631CF5BEB156.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.

3FB4E21B585B45AE9B29327C70ED7AC4.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

46EEAB310F034779AE80D8B9FB529D20.description: Use Key Ideas and Details to:

741E76AAAD0244B6B72887D24BB014B0.description: Apply strategies to comprehend and interpret literary texts.

3B2C8BA93DD64F05B3AB4558E99A250C.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (for example: presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (for example: small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

A1CEEB3EF0A54B008E69E2C6425BBFEF.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

B6D03B1F91B34315945B6EB9A88DDCE6.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

07ED76B625F142A489564B62732AF13E.description: Create a plan to effectively present information both informally and formally.

F3A82F00C40146C3905D321EFA52F673.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points

C094DADB521340BF8772456AF2046B71.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

2708B10C486F4DEA82A4922C132775FC.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

F0709F458EBE41018AB623CF007361F9.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

CD525367723C44BBA82843A2C4571647.description: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:

2F0109DDDBD2466DA9DEDDB2723037E2.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

7D710D1BEFD84365B02E96A092596F96.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

E3E624047E494B31BE134EBB10946C61.description: Interpret and evaluate complex informational texts using various critical reading strategies.

93D729B7486A4166A215D4997984D23B.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 11-CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

5A55F6B9E84A4BF0813A7ACE0A4F1FD6.description: By the end of 12th grade, analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (for example: recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. 15F5C29CCAC94617999AE00BAA667A18.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

F45EBEF3CBEA420E9F0215D3E8448E20.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text.

9C8E1FD9CF274D68A17B995CDB573CC1.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.
