experiences related to the target language and its cultures when using the
three modes at the advanced-low range.

871FFF6C58454B508C31071526675ADF.description: Evaluate information gathered from target language resources connected to other content areas.

416E50229F9842E5BE81C91F9F76F24C.description:
Connections: Connect with other disciplines and acquire information and
diverse perspectives in order to use the language to function in academic and career-related situations.

D78EC919A1A7403EBC14DF2F5AB2275F.description:
Interact at a competent level in familiar and some unfamiliar cultural
contexts when using the target language in the three modes at the
advanced-low range.

1FCDB71986E84C03B6FB94EB3CC9C7FB.description:
Demonstrate awareness of subtle differences among cultural behaviors and
adjust the student’s behavior accordingly, in familiar and some unfamiliar
situations when using the target language in the three modes at the
advanced-low range.

A0FF6681B6234611BAB434D930D60574.description:
Converse comfortably with others from the target culture, in familiar and
some unfamiliar situations and show some understanding of cultural
differences when using the target language in the three modes at the
advanced-low range.

7FA670F01C7242808A62C3CC945F4857.description:
Explain how a variety of products of public and personal interest are related
to perspectives when using the target language in the three modes at the
advanced-low range.

B0BAB266DE9B49048DEBB5483F2E4921.description: Explain some diversity among products and how it relates to perspectives in the target cultures and the student’s own.

2742EDBBB5A743D3AB2E75D6A770A17D.description:
Interact at a competent level in familiar and some unfamiliar cultural
contexts when using the target language in the three modes at the
advanced-low range.

04EA7D8735AE4420995936CC9C744912.description:
Demonstrate awareness of subtle differences among cultural behaviors and
adjust the student’s behavior accordingly in familiar and some unfamiliar
situations when using the target language in the three modes at the
advanced-low range.

1779A1682D63464DA2947342EDFF693A.description:
Converse comfortably with others from the target culture in familiar and
some unfamiliar situations and show some understanding of cultural
differences when using the target language in the three modes at the
advanced-low range.

5FEB13A1CEA14DA8BAA5C4BE9087B5F3.description:
Explain how a variety of practices within familiar and social situations are
related to perspectives when using the target language in the three modes
at the advanced-low range.

C6744AD1351E40D0B696CFE3A6FF4EB2.description: Explain some diversity among practices and how it relates to perspectives in the target cultures and the student’s own.

50628A1C6C934A4BB565EA70C3C82192.description:
Cultures/Intercultural Communication:
Interact with cultural competence and understanding.

7794EB4514974EA89D3D0D1D648FAD59.description:
Deliver presentations on some concrete academic, social and professional
topics of interest, using paragraphs across major time frames.

156646AD65F04B85BF567D5673CB22AF.description:
State a viewpoint with supporting evidence on some concrete academic,
social and professional topics of interest, using paragraphs across major
time frames.

E5F7D97A2744465BA6BF06A6EE4290C0.description:
Tell stories about school and community events and personal experiences,
using paragraphs across major time frames.

62BB34B43EC64DB9A3C48CC7605EE065.description:
Deliver detailed and organized presentations on familiar as well as unfamiliar concrete topics, in paragraphs and using various time
frames through spoken, written or signed language (presentational mode).

DA27C439926B449597E85C1443905F65.description:
Identify the underlying message and some supporting details in
conversations and discussions across time frames.

8CBCB8A9496645E0AD6D39943BD982CF.description:
Identify the underlying message and some supporting details in fictional
texts across time frames.

3715354276CD4ED7B0D9D42D0BBEB59F.description:
Identify the underlying message and some supporting details in descriptive
informational texts across time frames.

E43C46DA18074EC983E8D012775B47BF.description:
Understand the main message and supporting details on a wide variety of familiar and general interest topics across various time frames
from complex, organized texts that are spoken, written or signed (interpretive mode).

7DA112B742AD40D6805053DB8A12EC4D.description:
Maintain conversations by providing explanations and comparisons of
preferences, opinions, and advice on familiar and concrete academic and
social topics using a few simple paragraphs across major time frames.

F6830740BB4B44BEB05A3F827D7EFA77.description:
Interact and negotiate to resolve an unexpected complication that arises in
a familiar situation, using a few simple paragraphs across major time
frames.

DDE5CBB31E2248C4B92682E0ADFB9F21.description:
Exchange information and ideas on a variety of familiar and concrete
academic and social topics, using a few simple paragraphs across major
time frames.

E97A134F3C844C0E97E1629EB59D8EFD.description:
Maintain spontaneous spoken, written or signed conversations and discussions across various time frames on familiar, as well as
unfamiliar, concrete topics, using series of connected sentences and probing questions (interpersonal mode).

B4126C9FDF3048D7AEA7F8C2415C37CB.description:
Communication: Communicate effectively in more than one
language in order to function in a variety of situations and for multiple purposes.

document.title: Colorado Department of Education 2019-2020 Academic Standards & EEOs

4712B531A84D49858CC303BB1AAA85BC.description:
Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles, and
use the nets to find the surface area of these figures.

DB574A34D43F478ABBF1EF3CD22EEB42.description: Create polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices.

BBEB5687EE6B4CE99FDFD66AA96EC509.description:
Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole number edge
lengths by packing it with unit cubes and show that the volume is the same
as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism.

CA15005718F0415CAC7532505A37DDB5.description:
Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and
mathematical problems.

6BF31F06AB9B42E1B1F6AEDA9F81061F.description:
Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, parallelograms, and
trapezoids by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and
other shapes.

DED1DD4C293B41038B571197C6D13A06.description: Geometry: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

CEBE994CF96F4BEE8E51AC1B3D532BA8.description: Interpret these values in a real-world context.

D57919273F3B48DEAA21F504E05B5B33.description:
Summarize numerical data sets by counting the number of observations,
identifying the largest and smallest observations, and informally identifying
observations near the center.

FCE76AFC77664CA894D23FDA55B9E972.description: Display data in plots on a number line, including dot plots and histograms.

040199718F954ED5B83444DF388BFF8D.description: Statistics & Probability: Summarize and describe distributions.

B34DBC348CC44EE2AA9B18E35A33BEDC.description:
Match given measures of center (mean or median) and variation (range) to
a display of a data distribution.

C1FAE9BEED0646B7B20FC6AF766C8AA3.description:
Match statistical questions to a distribution of data that can be described by
its center, spread, and overall shape.

80A2C1D1799E4F43804578E031AFD1AA.description:
Match statistical questions to appropriate sources of data. For example,
match the question, “How tall are 6th graders?” to a sample of 6th grade
students.

7C70C1DBA03D4D92B80CA26EEF0A76F3.description: Statistics & Probability: Develop understanding of statistical variability.

E59DAE7F9B854954A82A62B4CAE86960.description:
For example, a table of people and shoes in the classroom might have a
column p, for people, and a column s, for shoes, and although the
number of people and shoes can vary, there is always twice as many
people as shoes.

194F1857BFA5401E89173B153B70A59F.description:
Analyze the relationship between variables using a table, such as a 2-
column table with on column labeled with each variable.

AFC511FF4F3244998EEADD35DF2BE02A.description:
Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that
change in relationship to one another.

DB7A5980C43D445B8478CD7BEB0CB9BB.description: Expressions & Equations: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

CBAFD5BD30BE43AC91595B6681FDA587.description:
For example, if you have more than 8 dollars, the inequality x > 8 would
be true for any amount of money (x) greater than 8 dollars.

FC7ADAF1D428468088C209DD9EC2E4B5.description:
Evaluate an inequality of the form x > c or x < c that represents a real-world
or mathematical problem.

C56E24074974417F8DDA5C2C99C13D1A.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems by solving equations of the
form x ± p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all whole
numbers.

D33134B2C43E43F1BA48A9A8C90385AE.description:
For example, a number of apples plus a number of bananas could match
the expression a + b.

EB4B145605974934AC9C46F3DE1A17D4.description: Identify or match an expression using variables to a real-world problem.

2DCC68F32D6B4E2387ABB3E802A73C73.description:
For example, for the equation 5x = 1-, does x = 1 make the equation
true? Does x = 2? x = 3? x = 4?

B82EEF80384A4858BF8FA2630B21B1E7.description:
Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set
makes an equation true.

58A90A7E194C4FDE9300A84BAC09A970.description:
Answer the question: Which values from a specified set make the equation
true?

80BE4F0B70F74D72952570A927EF9EB8.description: Expressions & Equations: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

0B5AF040CEA8499BA17CD958B1E65F15.description:
For example, the expressions y + y + y and 3y are equivalent because
they name the same number regardless of which number y stands for.

4DC40B5FF49B426CA4D48171228C2747.description:
Identify when two expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the two
expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted
into them).

C8187FD4960F4EBF923D63E577A9A2E5.description:
For example, apply the distributive property to the expression 3(2 + 4)
to identify the equivalent expression 6 + 12.

6F5A131648EB419FA5114F51759BB217.description:
Apply the properties of operations to identify given equivalent expressions
using single-digit integers.

BCF108EE6E44433FBCF2233495948766.description:
For example, if x = 4, x + 1 should be interpreted as 4 + 1, which has a
value of 5.

73A6E56836F24405BF88FA0373B65FF2.description: Perform arithmetic operations in the conventional order.

5C114D10BEAA40F180519D8710BBC3C9.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables.

B376A49572AD4DAAA189BB63A9ABA051.description:
Identify parts of an expression that indicate operations (add, subtract,
multiply, divide).

E1252B12C4DF48C58E65480B0A2A9641.description: Read and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

80D7349CB49E44699E1545322EFBABF6.description:
Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving single-digit integer
factors, like -4 x 3 can mean 3 groups of -4, which totals -12.

63B5D66DD32045B8A0CBCC7834AB2D7A.description: Expressions & Equations: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

CE7A58C5E38B448F9C9250C780FC01EF.description:
For example, if Shelby lives at 1st St. and 6th Ave., and Lisa les at 4th St.
and 6th Ave., how many blocks away from each other do they live?

D9D768A81095450DB1AD8A2D884439CD.description:
Find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the
same second coordinate.

FAC1A27D11614A60872746D425E84CEF.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems represented by graphed
integer-coordinate points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane.

0CDA9A48D1524B6A95D935B343BD8648.description:
Relate negative values to a real-world situation, such as -2 could
represent owing someone two dollars.

4B032F76DFD54E72A1370A029018F829.description:
For example, identify that -2 is greater than -5 because -2 is located to
the right of -5 on a number line.

3BC8DD4B947C421B9BDEF3DF24D22A4F.description:
Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative
position of two numbers on a number line diagram.

5CF837EBD6514FDDBA9FB85FBFF8A430.description: Order and find absolute value of integers between -10 and 10.

1E44FA49D690488DA9A50A1AAD9AFF7B.description: Find and position pairs of integers on a coordinate plane.

CF7D984129AB4829AD58C4FAA1151CC5.description:
Find and position integers on a horizontal or vertical number line
diagram.

9CDE12F4EFBB4755B019935E50CE657E.description:
Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in
quadrants of the coordinate plane.

275CC495021440A7823241FD2887A229.description:
Use opposite signs of numbers indicating locations on opposite sides of
0 on the number line.

DFC9636F50454E6B9C75963933CDED0F.description:
Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from
previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with
negative integer coordinates.

D67EED4609E242DA94F518B9F373269F.description: Identify integers on a number line.

D7E58E5ECF1044DE85B1BD2E598126C7.description:
Identify positive and negative numbers that are used together to describe
quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature
above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits,
positive/negative electric charge).

EB7143BC800B4F03AC5D9A4126FAD800.description: The Number System: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

27528307B2AD4497AC99BE8E2CE92248.description:
For example, if there are 8 hot dogs in a package and 6 buns in a
package, how many packages of each do you buy to not have hot dogs
or buns left over?

E8C9C90F2975452FA3FB37340A57E34D.description:
Find common factors of two whole numbers less than or equal to 20 and
common multiples of two whole numbers less than or equal to 10.

2A963EC2C8C04E4C9030979A4D5DCE01.description: For example, do simple calculations with amounts of money.

314BA9DF0EDC4702856332BFD2EB462F.description:
Add, subtract, multiply, and divide numbers less than ten with one or two
decimal places using appropriate strategies for each operation and/or a
calculator.

DBF61221AB7F465397EF4A276B8D333E.description:
For example, students can divide 36 cookies into 12 boxes by counting
out one cookie per box until there are 3 in each box.

E7EF343C275F4DA08277A4459CFD6E0A.description:
Divide multi-digit numbers using illustrations or demonstrations of fair
share and equal share strategies.

56A2EF90BDEB4C2DB614999FEC0AE0D4.description: The Number System: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

90820F1C9487437F879F4A96754EEEE2.description:
Illustrate quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division
of a larger benchmark fraction by a smaller benchmark fraction resulting in
whole-number quotients, e.g., by using visual fraction models to represent
division in problems like 3 divided by 1
.

3DAFF1D5581E4809B9BFFA11FD963725.description: The Number System: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

970F749746314C5CBBA8C4FBDBBAFA53.description:
For example, students should be able to make a table relating the two
socks they wear each day and use that to find the number of socks they
need for a 3-day trip.

579DBE7056BE4ACA95AAD069E0EBDC05.description:
Equivalent ratios should be simple, like 1:2 is equivalent to 2:4, or 2:3 is
equivalent to 4:6.

9123779D01814834A18610F92A928225.description:
Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world problems, e.g., by
reasoning about tables of equivalent rations.

F6BE8364966E4B2C9D837B3E5067452A.description:
For example, student uses ‘per’ and ‘for each’ language, such as “There
are 24 hours for each day” or “There are two gloves per student.”
(Expectations for unit rates in this grade are limited to non-complex
fractions)

12393B6A2DEA4A81A33906D0DF9EA351.description:
Apply the concept of a unit rate and use rate language and/or written
representations in the context of a ratio relationship.

3635FF635A6044058DCC7C62775A8581.description:
For example, count out two shoes for each one person, or indicate there
are four wheels for each car in the parking lot.

092D4251446048C1A9E79CCA469218AC.description:
Apply the concept of a ratio and use ratio language or actions to describe a
ratio relationship between two quantities up to at least 5 each.

62FF653416F0458FA0C2F4D6968982B2.description: Ratios & Proportional Relationships: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

document.title: Colorado Department of Education 2019-2020 Academic Standards & EEOs

09310F99EA064B07BAD5424CBA73E2EB.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the area of triangles,
rectangles, and circles, and the volume and surface area of right rectangular
prisms.

B074C467ACB344CDADBF569883DC00B3.description: Recognize angles that are acute, obtuse, and right (EE.7.G.B.5).

7479F0A8CB844544BB71BE7E5A21CF2C.description:
Use the formula for the area and circumference of a circle to solve
problems.

3A5FCCF640F64E949D8D90D42D438CCF.description: Geometry: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

6921F93685B54828991095E569FE3018.description: Describe rectangular cross-sections from right rectangular prisms.

F07E80BEF2BE4401BC2DDCFEA959640B.description:
Create triangles with given conditions and recognize that some
combinations of side lengths and/or angles cannot be made into a triangle.

216E79A360BA48FEACEB59092C526EDD.description:
Match corresponding parts of scale drawings of geometric figures and
compare given lengths and areas.

735D11E8CE0047B0A824B8B0E504BC79.description: Geometry: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

DE9F6D39DBD84404B4C62E8CFE30EEA0.description:
Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists and tree
diagrams.

229858FF0AA54890BB1097907B16DB9C.description:
For example, given that the probability of flipping heads is 0.5, getting 8
heads out of 10 flips is not good agreement with the model.

E533A5EBC5D74081BA3AEE772F464C8D.description:
Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies and identify
when agreement is not good.

39F3CF156E57493EBD0E713822B89A55.description:
Collect data on a chance process (e.g., flipping a coin, rolling a die) and
observe its long-run relative frequency.

B2C85EB393044ADEA0243D73F834A036.description:
Indicate an understanding that the probability of a chance event can be 0,
for things that never happen, between 0 and 1, for things that sometimes
happen, or 1, for things that always happen.

A4E60411FCE44D2AAED21AB40FD13AF8.description: Statistics & Probability: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

7F0D3EF1383B4E1C9DD814B328259AFE.description:
For example, if the average height of a class of 8th graders is 5 feet 5
inches, and the average height of a class of 7th graders is 5 feet 2 inches,
which population is more likely taller on average, 8th graders of 7th
graders?

30C7EF783F124689A07AD917B0A49664.description:
Use given measures of center and given measures of variability for
numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative
inferences about two populations.

68E039447A7849EDA2578DEF975BDF03.description:
Informally compare two sets of data within a single data display, such as a
picture graph, line plot, or bar graph.

FFDA21FA6CEA428896FEA0D07225988C.description: Statistics & Probability: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

7F8AA51CFD8C4F4089B840544740BC90.description:
For example, conclude from a sample of the class that most students
like chocolate ice cream.

AF08F2A2992144B5BAF6CE0FB992FDC3.description: Use data from a sample to answer a statistical question.

E47BF64CA8554C7899571CB6686BFF12.description:
Understand that statistics usually involves measuring something about a
sample to learn something about a problem.

5C04025AE7FF4BEC93B9993D6D9C81B3.description: Statistics & Probability: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

F912D1BB25124ED3AE9B4138C44D36E1.description:
Represent the problems using objects or drawings and match the
situations to equations (in this case, x + 2 = 8).

3C44656E511142DBABAB0673E6A073FA.description:
For example, if x number of glasses of water plus 2 glasses of water
makes 8 glasses of water total, then x must be 6 glasses of water.

1F833C0E4A124600BCDBF00C3DB27D5E.description:
Solve real-world or mathematical problems using simple equations
containing variables.

268A8C7B7A104BA4BCCF89AA4AB03BAD.description:
For example, if a sandwich costs $6.50 and a drink costs $1.50, but you
have a coupon to save 1 off the total, how much will you spend for the 4
sandwich and the drink?

00B1410C19C84FB2AFB80F27356A2AF0.description:
Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with whole
numbers, benchmark fractions, and/or decimals to two decimal places.
Numbers should combine cleanly for simpler calculations.

F9A9B782DDF249B08610E53795ECA622.description: Expressions & Equations: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

8894926A2B8D4E869368F5B1F0E47B31.description:
For example, if 3 people at lunch spend $21 for sandwiches, the
expression $7 x 3 tells us that it was 7 dollars for each of the 3
sandwiches.

FEC3D1DFE3194102A27BA3E9736A9C93.description:
Demonstrate that rewriting an expression in different forms can shed light
on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.

3E5EE2C35B164B65A2DD311757EB6107.description:
Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract linear
expressions with whole number coefficients. For example, 2x + 3x is 5x.

EDB597266B364F5BA0CF0222A47E2146.description: Expressions & Equations: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

43DFD92129734506AC3C62189B6718BD.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations.

2D2E1E443CCD4BB2A6E05F8950855AD0.description:
For example, dividing 3 of a pizza into pieces the size of 1 of the whole 4 4
pizza can be written as 3 divided by 1
, and it yields 3 pieces.

89528628251C4666B47D9D3F0364FAE1.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division
and or fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers with single-digit
numerators and denominators up to at least 12, e.g., by using visual
fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

F41F5C2CC32541EA9061E38064307244.description:
Represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number
line diagram. For example, add -
1 +
3
 to get 1
.

B06646EB4A9947A09630D7E09809B65E.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to
add and subtract rational numbers with single-digit numerators and
denominators up to at least 12.

E866AD7E4E5E4AB1B7F34416ED446A80.description:
The Number System: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide
rational numbers.

4C6764C4C72548C8A30F827415E2F3DF.description: Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, and gratuities.

994862D3E25E4B768A615C1C2AE3F8D9.description: Use proportional relationships to solve simple ratio and percent problems.

E766C8108F8F4F70A2AD11149CE48F12.description: Represent proportional relationships between quantities using a table.

0FB36A49783342F1AF42A30A088F7A14.description:
For example, if a person walks 6 miles in 2 hours, compute the unit rate
as the fraction 6
, equivalently 3 miles per hour.

42BD8FC250264CA0A742DF93B9FA59B3.description:
Compute unit rates associated with ratios of whole numbers, including
ratios of lengths, areas, and other quantities measured in like or different
units.

89BF654CA9AD4B57A65237E84B8EDD39.description:
Ratios & Proportional Relationships: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical
problems.

document.title: Colorado Department of Education 2019-2020 Academic Standards & EEOs

200098E28BBC4C0A844CC52D51376E52.description:
Use the formulas for the volumes of cylinders to solve real-world and
mathematical problems.

7E9874C9C1F44EB3897AB812143C0456.description: Geometry: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

8E08CEB26F1A4D98A560413BF49419CD.description: Measure to find the distance between two points on a coordinate plane.

1066FA140E3D4C37AF7F95F113D6C81D.description:
Represent a right triangle on a coordinate plan and measure to find missing
side lengths.

A1675B51991942A1B3349DF5C6B206CB.description:
Explain or otherwise demonstrate how the areas of the squares constructed
on the sides of a 3-4-5 right triangle correspond to the parts of the formula
for the Pythagorean Theorem.

FD9CFC09759B41BFB3D29ED5D6216CB0.description: Geometry: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

587B09A35F444C29BA89CDCF1801484E.description:
Use angle measurements to establish facts about the angle sum of triangles
and about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal

8C014EE1296840A68117D01AF3285457.description:
Recognize that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second
can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections,
translations, and dilations.

253BFDD4CFD749FF82E7A5484B52A717.description:
Describe the effect of a translation, rotation, or reflection in the coordinate
plane by matching a point on the figure with the corresponding point on the
image of the future.

82F9074852324808947FC5A12D8A1B64.description:
Demonstrate congruence of two-dimensional shapes by rotating, reflecting,
and/or translating one shape onto another.

8E858D024DD84B25933C95209E3AF838.description: Geometry: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

FBEF77DAC7EC4576905DDB4C2119C20F.description:
Construct a graph or table from given categorical data and compare the
data categorized in the graph or table.

9D57ED458A6C4210B0FCB92D15ECCA86.description:
Use a graph of linear model in the context of bivariate measurement data

E2D59E0569E1409782E8C713DE66375D.description:
For example, for a sequence defined by the rule “Add 5 starting at 0,”
match the 3rd place with the value 15.

E382EAF7F7E44B6BAF8F3FB6D6F18F38.description: Match the place in a sequence with the value in the sequence.

8320B83C6B29455ABA7F4EBA6C84CC92.description: Evaluate functions for inputs in their domains.

EDA14C87C6454B5DA12E974F2748ECEF.description:
Demonstrate an understanding that a function is a correspondence from
one set to another set.

1CF3808501524F15A63605AF6FBE88DD.description: Interpreting Functions: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

2F5D9A281E594AEDACCB48817CDDA2FC.description:
For example, the line d = 50h could represent distance traveled when
moving at 50 miles per hour. The point (2,100) represents traveling 100
miles after 2 hours).

BE50F49277B94CC6BEEDC4AA69954735.description: Interpret the meaning of a point on a graphed line in context.

4C5697FB39974EAC8F29720BFCBBBFC6.description:
Confirm that the point of intersection for a given system of linear equations
is the point that makes both equations true.

AFC30CFBF974487BB92C7B443A7C0195.description: Graph an equation in two variables given a table of values.

8E78F9AE59294E4FBA61B544518FAD14.description: Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

4E4ECF15DD8E40DF9865FAE0EE12044B.description:
Solve systems of linear equations approximately with graphs, focusing on
pairs of linear equations in two variable.

FBDD7B275FAA47E28DC63EC4FB6513EE.description: Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities: Solve systems of equations.

282A7B9D0C264C0EB4DBEA8C9E8C8DEC.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

A0077E53ADBF49EFA4D75A49118AEB35.description: Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

684D2948AE7148AE8344EE91EC8F9E01.description:
Explain each step in solving a simple given equation involving one or two
operations, such as 3x + 1 = 7 (Step 1), 3x = 6 (Step 2), and x = 2 (Step 3).

7A0AB30362694F2F99A591923FE7AA6E.description: Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

18CDBD31F33C4755A16C7ABDA523603B.description:
For example, if the speed limit is 70 miles per hour and you have 4 hours
of travel time, destinations less than or equal to 280 miles away are
going to be possible to reach in that time. Destinations greater than 280
miles away are not.

FBDB720A149945268444A092670AAC89.description: Identify solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.

D3F335162F3F4302BC30AE386B0E9BFE.description:
Create equations in two variables to represent linear relationships between
quantities and graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

45F0135F59664AF4B292149E83E45407.description: Include equations arising from linear functions.

966C97825E494330BCC2969845C0B54E.description:
Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve
problems.

2C393B0CA74A43DFA5AC5658E05DACB5.description: Creating Equations: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.★

6672BA0E9C1E4967800337183D2F577C.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions: Rewrite rational expressions.

D77370861AA84050B4568690A3236540.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

6F4DAC8CCEE34AA68E6BD1F17D7F97D6.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

E528174B05654246BC633C424938C6F4.description: Add and subtract first-degree polynomials, i.e., combine like terms.

EB5D32ED936E46ADB0FC0CE7DF56B24F.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions: Perform arithmetic operations on polynomials.

F764388A5A3942D09BBFA4441D3F2B8A.description:
Determine the successive term in a geometric sequence given the common
ration (EE.A.SSE.4).

0F28A23765CB485E9165205041F2B49C.description:
For example, 80w + 20w + 200 + 300 might describe earning $80 per
week at one job and $20 per week at another job, as well as one-time
gifts of $200 from a parent and $300 from a grandparent. That could be
re-written in the equivalent form as 100w + 500, which would then help
show the total earned per week ($100) and the sum of the one-time
gifts ($500).

973627DD04444ACAAC9A452E723D3BFF.description:
Choose and produce an equivalent form of a one-variable expression to
reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the
expression.

3B18A45B2D4D47C2A6959A93A2C15813.description: Seeing Structure in Expressions: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

F3B0F738E1054A72868E59F0F081D4B0.description: For example, 3x can be written as x + x + x.

E1DFF1AC21FF4EBCA304D468DFCEA55F.description: Use the structure of a simple expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

EB8957561FFA4A1BAD63B85C641F9B43.description:
For example, the expression 100w + 500 could represent earning $100
per week (w) and a starting balance of $500.

7A7AD51581E6413EAD13DE383DE312D6.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

1CF0BCC932BF4FB5ADF5F138C7145331.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

5214E3F6B2244C01B2218D6B333A8E96.description: Seeing Structure in Expressions: Interpret the structure of expressions.

90D6C3A429694EB8899081A264D4EA17.description: Vector & Matrix Quantities: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.

1D39F65E866C4088846592960EF21AD1.description: Vector & Matrix Quantities: Perform operations on vectors.

02032B07C36547D8BEA9FE218081C5CF.description: Vector & Matrix Quantities: Represent and model with vector quantities.

D922C21ABA3843ECBF695A6828E2DFDA.description:
Solve real-world problems with real coefficients that have real number
solutions.

A397EBFEE55C497F881748749588E7A6.description: The Complex Number System: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

83A3F2E36DC74814B2933A26135FFC7D.description: The Complex Number System: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.

2FEF327C78DF488285A64EC7C64AA932.description:
Use the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add,
subtract, and multiple real (whole) numbers (EE.C-CN.2.a).

E68CE0BCF959402B9655DDAF622BBBC8.description:
For example, we need the counting numbers to count whole things,
fractions and decimals to represent parts of wholes (or between wholes
on the number line), and negative numbers to represent quantities less
than zero.

E9ACA5124D464406825C6772FFCF496E.description:
Know that different kinds of numbers are needed to represent different
quantities.

7E1CF1F006F3484FAEAE7CEEA142371D.description: The Complex Number System: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

A0BCC99A4AEB4640BB6BA7B9465CA7D9.description:
For example, students should be able to give an example of when
knowing time to a fraction of a second (like running in a race) versus the
nearest year (like giving your age).

EEB5F6CE71D8410EB186E39D8BA52DA4.description:
Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement
when reporting quantities.

045B14149E0D487BBB012BDD00C966B9.description:
For example, fuel economy can be described as miles per gallon (instead
of feet per barrel of gasoline) because miles and gallons are the way we
typically measure driving distances and fuel use.

91764450045149F5BE5722FBE7ECE875.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

1EB0F2A053F2474BAA36B306996BEBA4.description:
For example, a problem asking “How many eggs will I use today if I’m
using half of three dozen eggs today and the other half tomorrow?”
requires a student to make sense of “dozen” either at the beginning (3
dozen is 36 eggs, and half is 18 eggs) or at the end (half of 3 dozen is 1.5
dozen, which is 18 eggs) of their solution.

40476FAB26784DEBAC0F3C5237B5EBFD.description:
Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of
multi-step problems.

16F1F3D0B9CC4A0EA6AD51EDACAF9A26.description: Quantities: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

F32504EBC34F4E5D8608D000D8811CE4.description: The Real Number System: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

C5C1543ED23D4E96BAAD057AE4140A0D.description:

form, e.g., y3 = y times y times y.

E9305DBC14374ADF97A7470B539321E5.description:
Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number
exponents of 2 or 3 (squared and cubed).

B6328B3EE1F649879E188A5C3A4D37DF.description: The Real Number System: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

document.title: Colorado Department of Education 2019-2020 Academic Standards & EEOs

85A657C382234046B14D2F5B3A4B1247.description:
Correctly follow directions involving their own position in space, such as
“stand up” and “move forward.”

2B508D3CECAE4EF0B36A037AE9024A13.description:
Indicate an understanding of language related to directionality, order, and
the position of objects, including up/down and in front/behind.

6FAE7BED8A9D4406B29DDDB0A8AE02FA.description: Geometry: Explore the positions of objects in space.

CA8250E8D56348C88135726F67B8703B.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.

9FA307AB22634EBAA5DDBE951041731E.description:

on a countable or measurable attribute (e.g., number of sides, corners).

05C6B5A2483149EB905084769F105A9D.description:
Identify basic shapes (circle, square, rectangle, triangle) having the same
orientation and size.

92CBC66F81A7406D88ED7C0B46DADF2D.description:
Indicate an understanding (e.g., by naming or sorting) of differences of
shapes in terms of length of sides, number of sides, and number of
angles/corners.

F6788803277345C399166859F410C340.description: Geometry: Identify, describe, compare, and compose shapes.

1A0FEAE3FFB24EE3866E41E537A613E7.description:
Measure using the same unit, such as putting together snap cubes, to see
how tall a book is.

406905D6EF33412993D95FEE78F56C5C.description:
Compare or order up to at least three objects based on their measurable
attributes, such as height or weight.

D14045AC84AE40A6B188C49A509C6F2A.description:
Indicate an understanding of comparative language, such as shortest,
heavier, biggest, or later.

914CFF512AAB49D38332AF11D0898168.description:
Measurement & Data: Measure objects by their various attributes using standard and nonstandard measurement and use
differences in attributes to make comparisons.

C172DA06DD3A431FA464ED3976B008E9.description:
Identify the core unit of sequentially repeating patterns, such as color in a
sequence of alternating red and blue blocks.

4D9325FACBDC485992B770D71F78E9E8.description:
Extend simple patterns. Example: Copy an ABAB pattern and extend it to
ABABAB.

6AAD97AA688B4437BF2D4E1801718038.description: Duplicate simple patterns in the same location as demonstrated.

F889CAA4B8814AD382016ED8E31E98FD.description:
Recognize a simple pattern by touching, pointing, or saying the pattern in
sequence without skipping elements.

811268E0124342D6B20C960FE605B331.description: Operations & Algebraic Thinking: Understand simple patterns.

15E81D5166D245DE804376D638815863.description:
Begin to use counting on (adding 1 or 2, for example) from the larger
number for addition.

A991FEFF5A9143EDAF9FB62655890309.description:
Examples: “If you have one block and I give you one more, how many
will you have?” “If you have three cookies and eat two, how many will
you have left?”

BD2A91555CFA48479E9F2B85B0708CC6.description:
Solve addition and subtraction problems set in simple contexts. Add and
subtract up to at least two, to or from, a given number to find a sum or
difference up to at least 5.

CE069200AC5D4F55B4C5730DF1F2F05C.description:
Represent addition and subtraction in different ways, such as fingers,
objects, and drawings, to add “one more” or “take away one.” (EE.K.OA.1).

FD2ACDC7F0784EC1AEB0C6327532BAF9.description: Operations & Algebraic Thinking: Understand addition as adding to and understand subtraction as taking away from.

EBB72043FC924C6CBC098E58D80B98F0.description:
Recognize and, with support or assistive technology, write some numerals
or an approximation of a numeral up to at least 3.

A57059C26526469EB803D6585B43E9FC.description: Associate a number of objects within a written numeral up to at least 3.

EFB611188DE94129AD77A96E75507BDB.description: Counting & Cardinality: Associate a quantity with written numerals up to 5 and begin to write numbers.

4D8334FDB9D144F6A2CD731ECB0BFDEF.description:
Identify and use numbers related to order or position from first to at least
third.

13D5D49F45914C1C8EA23AF0283027BC.description: Example comparisons include 1 vs. 4, 5 vs. 2, and 3 vs. 3 (EE.K.CC.6).

C994A96A8D534332897C3CE90A833057.description: Groups should be small and differences should be clear.

3F3A93313CFC446D96FFB9B75930AE9E.description:
Identify whether the number of objects in one group is more than, less
than, or the same as the number objects in another group.

A686725CE7A54D92A410C3BC58082617.description:
Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is
one larger.

A2D392D3D299405393684C0427D55074.description:
Accurately count as many as three objects in a scattered configuration or
out of a collection of more than four objects.

503A6726C96044D8B0E27A5A158831CB.description:
Use the number name of the last object counted to answer “How many?”
questions for up to at least 5 objects.

D77EC87621F643719D60C4D536FA55EA.description:
Identify the number names in order when counting, pairing one number
word that corresponds with one object, up to at least 5.

4B2295B4BC29403EB5D871C53D875EC4.description: Counting & Cardinality: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities.

C839C59BFD40407AAA4D17BE68EC5FF3.description:
Instantly recognize, without counting, small quantities of up to at least
three objects and indicate the number.

C26172920EB3453FB3784745F2F2D5DD.description: Counting & Cardinality: Recognize the number of objects in a small set.

2020A3A3447D452D9426B7CAFA2226BF.description: Count up to at least 5 by ones.

C269503EFB214C73A52E55AD082100B8.description: Counting & Cardinality: Know number names and the count sequence.
